SEARCH

Uses of Package
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa

Packages that use com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa
Package
Description
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.implicit
OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628) for input-constrained clients, such as a command line tool: the protocol customizer that wires the device authorization and verification endpoints, the guard that applies the multi-factor policy and the limit on the attempts to the verification endpoint, and the verification page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa
Multi-factor authentication orchestration.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott
One-time token authentication: e-mail and SMS codes and magic links as a primary sign-in method and as a second factor, the per-channel factors, the rate limits, the providers and filters, and the phone management API and account page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys
Passkeys (WebAuthn): the factor, the chain wiring, the login and second-factor fragments, the account API and the account page.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social
Social login (identity brokering) through external identity providers: Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Apple and GitHub.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.totp
Time-based one-time password (TOTP) second factor.
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509
X.509 client certificate authentication: a certificate presented on a dedicated TLS port, or forwarded by a trusted reverse proxy in a header, signs in the user it is bound to (by the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate) at POST /login/x509, the form of the login page, with the CSRF token.
  • Classes in com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa used by com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.implicit
    Class
    Description
    MfaAuthorizationManager
    Decides whether an authentication has presented enough factors for the request being served: when the client or the user requires multi-factor authentication, the factors must satisfy the MfaPolicy; otherwise any authentication does.
    ReauthenticationEntryPoint
    Forces a new sign-in: it discards the stale authentication of the session (the security context of the thread and the one stored by the repository), saves the request being served (typically /oauth2/authorize?...) so it resumes once the user has signed in again, and redirects to the login page.
    SecondFactorRequiredEntryPoint
    Sends a user who has presented a primary factor but not yet the second one to the second-factor page, after saving the request being served (typically /oauth2/authorize?...) so the sign-in resumes where it left off once the second factor is verified.
  • Classes in com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa used by com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa
    Class
    Description
    AuthenticationFactorRegistry
    Registry of the authentication factors this server knows.
    CurrentAccount
    The account an API request is made on behalf of: the owner of the bearer token.
    CurrentAccountResolver
    Resolves the account of the request being handled.
    FactorGrantor
    Adds the authority of a verified factor to an authentication.
    FactorTimeline
    Reads, from the FactorGrantedAuthority instances of an authentication, the factors that prove something about it and when they were presented.
    InsufficientUserAuthenticationException
    Thrown by StepUpGuard when the bearer token of an API call does not show a recent enough multi-factor sign-in for the operation.
    MfaAuthorizationManager
    Decides whether an authentication has presented enough factors for the request being served: when the client or the user requires multi-factor authentication, the factors must satisfy the MfaPolicy; otherwise any authentication does.
    ReauthenticationEntryPoint
    Forces a new sign-in: it discards the stale authentication of the session (the security context of the thread and the one stored by the repository), saves the request being served (typically /oauth2/authorize?...) so it resumes once the user has signed in again, and redirects to the login page.
    SecondFactorFragment
    Extension point that lets a second factor contribute a Thymeleaf fragment to the second-factor page.
    SecondFactorRequiredEntryPoint
    Sends a user who has presented a primary factor but not yet the second one to the second-factor page, after saving the request being served (typically /oauth2/authorize?...) so the sign-in resumes where it left off once the second factor is verified.
    SecondFactorRequiredException
    Raised while an authorization request is validated when the user must present a second factor first.
    SecondFactorUserResolver
    Resolves the identifier of the account of a signed-in user.
    StepUpGuard
    Guards the API operations that remove or reset a second factor (disabling the authenticator app, generating new recovery codes, revoking a trusted device): a stolen token, or a session left open, must not be enough to weaken the account.
    TrustedDeviceDtoMapper
    Maps the trusted devices of the domain onto the DTO generated from the contract, so a domain model is never returned from TrustedDeviceController.
    TrustedDeviceNotFoundException
    Thrown when an account has no trusted device with the requested identifier.
